hook: SCP-914 is a machine, a dial with five settings and a test log, and that is all it needs. Before reading the results, try guessing what each setting does to an ordinary object. Half the fun is checking your guesses.
whyItMatters:
914 is one of the most influential experiment-log SCPs. Its simple input and output structure invites readers to imagine their own tests, and the article itself opens that door with a closing note asking for more test data and a link to a separate experiment log hub. It also became a hands-on mechanic in SCP - Containment Breach, where players feed items into the machine.

It is credited to Dr Gears, who is also credited on SCP-106 and SCP-682, and the closing note quotes an in-universe "Dr. Gears" setting the testing rules, another case of an early author stepping into the setting.
thingsToNotice:
The test log is paced like a joke with a building punchline: steel becomes screws, then tacks, then something impossible. The machine's idea of refinement is literal and unpredictable, which is why a phone of a different model or a mouse of a different color is as unsettling as it is funny.

Then the biological tests change the tone. The article doesn't dwell on details; it reports the outcomes in a few dry lines and shuts the program down. That restraint lets you understand why the warning at the top exists without needing to show more.

related.note: Another simple-interface machine whose appeal lies in imagining what you would ask of it.
Also credited to Dr Gears; the same era's writing turned toward pure horror.
